items.text: AuDHD isn't red + blue. It's the colour that emerges when they mix. You can't predict it by adding the diagnoses. You have to see what shade you actually are.
items.rationale: The tie-dye metaphor from the source does all the work in one image. Quotable, self-contained, no overreach. Validates the 'I don't fit either stereotype' experience without claiming clinical novelty.

items.text: Craving routine and novelty at the same time. Sensory-seeking and sensory-avoidant. If you're AuDHD and nothing fits neatly — that's not a gap in your self-knowledge. That's the condition.
items.rationale: Names the internal contradictions AuDHD people live with daily. Pairs with the micro-insight above but stands entirely alone. No prescriptive claims, pure recognition.

items.text: Autistic burnout isn't depression that hasn't responded to treatment. It's your nervous system saying the environment is wrong. Rest helps. The environment has to change too.
items.rationale: Anchored to the 2026 Bougoure et al. psychometric validation study — the strongest evidence in this briefing. Directly validates the years-of-misdiagnosis experience without disparaging depression as a condition.
items.sensitivity_flag: Framing burnout as 'not depression' could implicitly devalue depression — monitor replies for that read. The distinction is peer-reviewed but the contrast is pointed. Consider whether 'related but different' framing would soften without losing the point.

items.text: Burnout recovery isn't just doing less. It's doing less of what you didn't choose. Rest without autonomy is managed exhaustion, not recovery.
items.rationale: Delivers the autonomy-restoration finding as a single, sticky reframe. Concrete and immediately applicable without prescribing a regimen — no medical-advice risk. Short and tight.

items.text: "School refusal" frames it as a choice — which frames the parent as enabling defiance. "School can't" names what's actually happening: a nervous system that cannot comply, regardless of want.
items.rationale: The language swap is the whole content. Shows precisely what the old term does wrong and what the new term does differently. No clinical overreach — locates the problem in terminology, not diagnosis.

items.text: If you've been told your child is "refusing" school and it doesn't feel like refusal to you — you're probably right. Can't and won't look the same from the outside. They aren't.
items.rationale: Direct address to parents experiencing the framing mismatch. Validates their lived read without overpromising, blaming professionals, or making a diagnostic claim.

items.text: Disclosure at work is the legal gateway to accommodations. It also makes you vulnerable in exactly the environment where vulnerability gets punished. That's not a mindset problem. It's a structural trap.
items.rationale: Names the bind precisely without giving advice or catastrophising. The 70% fear-of-disclosure figure from the Understood 2026 n=2,000+ survey grounds this as a documented pattern, not anecdote.
items.sensitivity_flag: 'Legal gateway' is US-ADA framing; disclosure rights and risks vary internationally. If the audience is global, soften to 'the official pathway to accommodations' to stay accurate.

items.text: If disclosing your neurodivergence at work meant you'd actually be supported — would you? And do you genuinely believe that would happen?
items.rationale: Two sentences, two questions. The first separates willingness from trust; the second opens the real tension. Earns replies because it's honest about the skepticism, not just validating.

items.text: Procrastination is a choice to delay. Task paralysis is when the start signal never fires — even when you want to begin and understand the stakes. They look the same. They are not the same.
items.rationale: The definitional contrast is the whole post. Immediate recognition value for anyone who has been frozen mid-intention. No prescriptive advice; creates space for the follow-on practical post.

items.text: "Just start" doesn't work for task paralysis because motivation isn't the problem — the launch signal is. Body doubling, external triggers, reducing the on-ramp. That's what actually helps.
items.rationale: Names why the ubiquitous advice fails, then offers three concrete, evidence-adjacent alternatives without promising outcomes or prescribing a regimen. Stands alone or follows the reframe post naturally.

items.text: PDA isn't defiance. It's an alarm. A nervous system interpreting demands as threat. You can't reset an alarm by raising your voice at it.
items.rationale: The alarm metaphor is crisp, memorable, and immediately implies the right intervention without stating it. Translatable across parents, teachers, and employers without condescension.

items.text: If every strategy you've tried is aimed at your child, you might be looking in the wrong place. A PDA child responds predictably to an overwhelming system. The system needs to change first.
items.rationale: Redirects the intervention target from child to environment. Validates exhausted parents who've tried everything while naming the real lever. 'Responds predictably' is load-bearing — it locates causality in the system, not the child or the parent.
items.sensitivity_flag: Direct address could land as parental blame even though the intent is opposite. Preview with a PDA parent in the community before publishing — the framing is defensible but the 'wrong place' line is pointed.
